correctness.rationale: For all s>=1, each strict-majority flip strictly lowers the bichromatic-edge count; only two fixed states exist, so almost-sure consensus holds. A complete case analysis for equal-one, equal-zero and opposite hubs yields the stated exact rational kernel, including all tie/threshold boundaries. A telescoping first-effective-update product proves the all-s formula; a second threshold calculation proves the parity edge correction and quarter limit. Three distinct exact-rational verifiers checked 35 count kernels, 8184 fully labelled states and 11 graph-edge comparisons.

value.rationale: Exact absorption probabilities for every deterministic initial state constitute a natural complete infinite-family classification of random sequential majority. In the polarized minority-versus-majority state, a fixed two-vertex minority has positive limiting win probability 1/4, and inserting a single hub edge changes selection probabilities precisely for odd leaf counts by (s+3)/((s+1)(s+2)). These probabilities and the parity-sensitive edge response are not determined by deterministic reachability alone and are motivated by information-cascade and small-influencer questions. Does not claim all fixation times or larger hub cliques.
